title: There is no verb "to have"
example_gloss: I have a cat. (literally: at me, [there] exists, a cat)
bridge_note: Possession isn't a verb you do in Russian — it's a location you're near. "Having" something is just that thing existing in your vicinity.

title: The word Nabokov said English couldn't translate
example_gloss: a deep spiritual anguish, often with no specific cause — Nabokov called it "a sensation of great spiritual anguish" that no single English word captures
bridge_note: It sits somewhere between longing, melancholy, and existential ache — close to all three, fully none of them.

title: There's no single verb for "to go"
example_gloss: go on foot one-way / go on foot habitually / go by vehicle one-way / go by vehicle habitually — four different verbs for what English calls just "go"
bridge_note: Russian has 14+ paired verbs of motion, splitting by manner (on foot vs. by vehicle) and by whether the trip is a single occurrence or a repeated/round-trip habit — English folds all of this into context and extra words.

title: A letter that makes no sound of its own
example_gloss: the "hard sign" — pronounced as nothing; it just blocks the consonant before it from softening
bridge_note: It's a purely grammatical instruction with zero sound of its own — the opposite of what a letter is usually for.

title: Everyone's middle name is literally "child of ___"
example_gloss: Ivan, son of Pyotr (Petrovich = "son of Pyotr") — used instead of Mr./Mrs. in formal address
bridge_note: Formal Russian address uses first name + patronymic together, no surname needed — it's simultaneously a name and a small family tree.

title: Numbers force the noun after them to change form
example_native: один стол, два стола, пять столов
example_gloss: one table, two tables, five tables — three different grammatical endings on "table," triggered purely by which number precedes it
bridge_note: 1 takes singular, 2-4 take a special "counting" form, 5+ take full plural genitive — the number itself dictates the noun's grammar, not just its meaning.
